clue.text: Stranger in Bali endeavours to fit in

indicators.note: the first 'in' tells us the answer sits inside the words that follow, spanning Bali and endeavours

explanation.surface: A foreigner on holiday in Bali tries hard to blend in with the locals.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the end of 'Bali' into the start of 'endeavours'; 'to fit in' is padding for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An alien is a foreigner, someone from another country or world.

clue.text: Predicament results from row with egghead

parts.note: a row is a fight or quarrel, a scrap
read as egg-head: the head (first letter) of egg

explanation.surface: Trouble follows a quarrel with an intellectual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' looks like an intellectual but is split as the head of 'egg'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is an awkward fix or tight spot one gets into.

parts.note: a steroid is a drug used to build up muscle

explanation.surface: An astronaut takes performance drugs to bulk up.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a rocky body that travels through outer space.

parts.note: to con is to swindle or cheat
a test is a trial or examination

explanation.surface: Someone disputes an accusation of cheating in a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: To contest a ruling is to dispute or question it.

indicators.note: translated suggests the letters of tsar's kin are converted into a new form

explanation.surface: An ancient tongue spoken by the Russian emperor's relatives is rendered into English.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the S of tsar's counts: TSARSKIN rearranges into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanskrit is the ancient classical tongue of India.

clue.text: Feeling it's been a huge success

explanation.surface: Someone describes how a triumph felt.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensation is both a physical perception and a smash hit that causes great excitement.

clue.text: Dangerous place rose lovers try to avoid

explanation.surface: Gardeners steer clear of a hazardous location.
explanation.walkthrough: Besides being a road accident hotspot, black spot is a fungal disease of roses.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident-prone stretch of road is so called, and the same name is a leaf fungus that plagues roses.

parts.note: ma is French for my, as a Parisian would say
bel is French for beautiful or lovely

explanation.surface: A Frenchman addresses his sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian' tells us both pieces are French: MA (my) and BEL (lovely).
explanation.definitionFit: Mabel is a female first name.

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
an amp (amplifier) helps you hear by boosting sound

explanation.surface: A big hearing device, yet weighing little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like the opposite of heavy, but is the definition as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp is a device that gives illumination.

clue.text: Dissolute old rebel leader sunk in depression

indicators.note: sunk in shows the rebel leader placed down inside the hollow

parts.note: a dent is a small hollow or depression
Jack Cade led a rebellion in England in 1450

explanation.surface: A dissipated former insurgent chief is down in the dumps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests low mood; it is a physical hollow. CADE is Jack Cade, leader of the 1450 Kentish revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent describes self-indulgent moral decline, as does dissolute.

clue.text: A ship is initially tempted to call for aid

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of the word tempted

explanation.surface: A vessel in trouble is first inclined to radio for help.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to help or give support.

clue.text: A man in the romantic mould

definitions.text: A man in the romantic mould

indicators.note: in signals that the answer is tucked inside the words that follow it, across the romantic

explanation.surface: A dashing, gallant fellow from a love story.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles 'the' and 'romantic'; 'mould' completes the surface, which also reads as a description of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A protagonist or brave champion is a male figure of this kind.

indicators.note: set, as in set out afresh, signals that spare tea is reordered

explanation.surface: A surplus tea service has been stored away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tea-set' looks like one thing, but 'Spare tea' is the anagram fodder and 'set' its indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate is to set apart or divide off.

clue.text: Idiot wants to impede the boss

parts.note: to block is to obstruct or impede
the head is the person in charge

explanation.surface: A fool sets out to obstruct his manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A blockhead is a dim-witted person, a dunce.

clue.text: Amazingly, Adam and Leo are in fashion

indicators.note: amazingly suggests the names Adam and Leo are jumbled in a surprising way

explanation.surface: Two men are surprisingly stylish dressers.
explanation.definitionFit: A la mode is a French borrowing meaning stylish or up to date.

explanation.surface: A wild region in north-west Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Mauritania means 'land of the Moors', so read cryptically it is a Moor land.
explanation.definitionFit: Open uncultivated upland is heath country; and the African country's name comes from the Moors' territory.

explanation.surface: A question about a halt in a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'channel' suggests water, but is a broadcasting channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway halt is one sense; a television or radio broadcaster is another.

indicators.note: set, as in rearranged, indicates the letters of ten traps are placed anew

explanation.surface: Someone lays traps inside a place of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: A transept is the cross arm of a cruciform church building.

indicators.note: read as re-served, the letters of claret I are served up again in a new order

explanation.surface: Perhaps a bottle of red wine I have put by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe a' defines by example: the word 'a' is the indefinite article in grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'a' is the indefinite type of this part of speech.

indicators.note: convey means carry, so the word for preferably carries the child inside it

parts.note: sooner means rather or preferably

explanation.surface: It would be better to send the youngster by sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a sailing vessel with fore-and-aft rigging.

explanation.surface: A grass sets out to annoy people.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a nark is a police informer, and to nark is to annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A police spy is one meaning; to irk or annoy someone is the verb sense.

indicators.note: from here means made out of, so the letters of Laos produce the answer

explanation.surface: In addition, it comes from a Southeast Asian country.
explanation.definitionFit: Also means in addition or besides.

clue.text: Plays for time in the theatre

explanation.surface: Someone procrastinating at a show.
explanation.walkthrough: The stalls are the ground-floor seats in a British theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To stall is to delay deliberately; the front ground-floor seating in a playhouse has the same name.

explanation.surface: Someone upholds the fortifications.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep is to preserve or hold; keeps are the strongest towers of castles.

clue.text: Anger caused by endlessly dire infection

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off the word for the disease

parts.note: cholera is a severe, often deadly infectious disease

explanation.surface: Rage provoked by a terrible disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Choler is an old word for irritability or wrath.

clue.text: Popular suit to a greater extent

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
spades is one of the four card suits

explanation.surface: A fashionable outfit, but more so.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in large amounts or to a high degree.

parts.note: little signals the abbreviation F for fellow
ain't is a colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A small man is not weak.
explanation.definitionFit: Faint means weak or barely perceptible.

clue.text: Gets furious about failure to find footwear

indicators.note: about indicates the word for losing one's temper goes around the failure

parts.note: to flip is to lose one's temper
a flop is a failure

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper when they cannot find their sandals.
explanation.definitionFit: These are light thong sandals.
